_about: Working brief map for the Telegram to remote processing to Anki feature. Statuses: KNOWN, INFERRED, ASSUMED, MISSING, CONTRADICTED.
title: Telegram-triggered remote German sentence workflow

slots.note: Make regular sentence capture frictionless while preserving the existing review-before-study boundary.
The user is the sole sender, reviewer, Anki account owner, and product approver; Codex is the implementation collaborator.
A researched feature brief for Telegram -> always-reachable server -> card enrichment -> staging -> approved cards in German Sentences v1 and the vocabulary ledger.
No hard deadline; sequence work as research and architecture decision, security design, then a five-sentence end-to-end pilot.
Capture happens in Telegram; processing and queue visibility live on the server portal. The user initiates Mac import, edits in Anki, and requests approval in the portal.

Use an installed Mac helper for user-triggered import and portal approval; never expose AnkiConnect or arbitrary commands. Proposed approval freezes the Browse selection locally, previews it in the portal, then commits only that unchanged set. Native confirmation policy remains open.
Forged webhook traffic, bot-token or AI-key leakage, exposing AnkiConnect, unsupported AnkiWeb automation, cross-machine delivery failures, duplicate cards, and silent approval bypass.
One authenticated learner using one Telegram bot and the existing German Anki profile/account.
Sentences are pasted locally; drafts are generated, staged through local AnkiConnect, reviewed in Anki Browse, and explicitly approved by ID or current Browse selection.
Each unique Telegram sentence produces exactly one editable staging item; approved items create the expected Study sentence and suspended ledger notes, with no duplicate or unauthorized writes.

MVP supports one authorized private bot chat, text messages, queue/status portal, user-triggered Mac import, Anki editing, and portal approval. Background polling, groups, media capture, multi-user tenancy, portal editing, and replacing Anki sync are deferred.

The design must handle corrected or incomplete German, duplicate Telegram updates, retries, server restarts, desktop offline periods, AI/TTS failures, malformed content, unauthorized senders, and partial import/approval.

The trusted Mac and Anki Desktop run periodically, not continuously. The server retains the queue; a user-initiated local pull module may launch Anki, wait for AnkiConnect, import safely, and acknowledge results.
Codex implements in this project; the user owns service accounts, hosting choices, credentials, content review, and acceptance.
Run a five-sentence pilot covering normal, corrected, duplicate, offline-desktop, and rejected-authorization cases; audit every transition before enabling daily use.
